advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify the token-never-logged test actually exercises the uvicorn.access request line (or clarify that only the synthetic-LogRecord test covers that sink).
evidence: TestClient is starlette/httpx-based (resolve_symbol confirms fastapi.testclient.TestClient) and does not run the uvicorn server / uvicorn.access logger, so no uvicorn access request-line record is ever emitted or captured here.
The ticket's leak is specifically in the `uvicorn.access` request line (ticket description shows `INFO: ... "POST /rerun?token=<secret>..."`), which this test path never produces.
advisory.finding: The header-auth 'token never logged' regression test uses FastAPI's TestClient + caplog, which captures the app's `rebar.*` logger records but never runs uvicorn's access-log path — the exact request-line sink where the leak occurs. It therefore cannot exercise or fail-on the real leak (uvicorn access line), so it does not truly cover AC 'the secret no longer appears in any log record the receiver emits'.
scenarios: A future regression that reintroduces the query token into the uvicorn access line would not be caught by this test, since the uvicorn access logger is not exercised.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a log-line assertion (or note the synthetic coverage) proving the query-string backward-compat path's token value is redacted in the emitted access line.
evidence: tests/unit/test_review_bot_token_redaction.py:164-168: the test posts `/webhook?token={SENTINEL}` and asserts only `resp.status_code == 202`.
The docstring itself states 'the redaction filter (option c) is what protects that value in the log', but no log assertion is made in this test.

test_webhook_still_accepts_query_token_for_backward_compat asserts only: `assert resp.status_code == 202, resp.text` (tests/unit/test_review_bot_token_redaction.py:168) — no assertion on the emitted log line for the driven query path.

Redaction is verified only against a synthetic record in _uvicorn_access_record with a hardcoded template `msg='%s - "%s %s HTTP/%s" %d'` (tests/unit/test_review_bot_token_redaction.py:41), not against a record produced by the running app.

ABSENCE: no test connects a driven `?token=` request to install_access_log_redaction()'s filter firing on the real emission; if the filter were attached to the wrong logger the synthetic-record tests would still pass and the backward-compat query path (which the change deliberately keeps alive) would still leak.
dropped.finding: test_webhook_still_accepts_query_token_for_backward_compat asserts only the 202 authentication result for the legacy query path; it does not assert the query token's value is scrubbed from the emitted access log — yet redaction of exactly that path is the stated purpose of option (c).
merged_from: No test drives a legacy ?token= request through the app and asserts the emitted uvicorn.access request line has the token scrubbed. The option-(c) redaction backstop is only proven against a hand-built synthetic LogRecord; the one test that drives a real query-string request (test_webhook_still_accepts_query_token_for_backward_compat) asserts only status_code == 202, never that the logged line is redacted. A misconfigured install (wrong logger) or a divergence between the synthetic record shape and uvicorn's real access record would let the backward-compat leak recur with every test still green — which is exactly the regression this change exists to prevent (ticket 66af Testing: 'drive a request carrying a known sentinel token through the app ... assert the sentinel does NOT appear in any emitted record ... verify RED by reverting').
scenarios: The backward-compat query path is authenticated but its log-redaction on a driven request is never asserted; only the synthetic LogRecord path validates redaction.
